Hi Aisha —

Appreciate the details and the load sample. Short answer: we can support a temporary concurrency uplift for the evaluation window, and we can offer a couple of packaging choices depending on whether you prefer time or committed consumption. Outline below: 

Option A — 7-day runway extension + temporary concurrency uplift (12 sessions):
- No additional monthly commitment; one-time evaluation surcharge of $1,800 for the uplift period.
- Keeps current trial token/usage billing as-is.
- SLA remains best-effort for trial systems.

Option B — 7-day extension + flexible credit bucket:
- We add a 25k token credit bundle for the extension period (covers the burst).
- No surcharge; credits are one-time and non-refundable.
- If you convert to a 3-month Pilot at the end of the trial, we’ll apply a $1,000 credit toward the committed capacity.

Option C — Timeboxed reserved mini-pilot (recommended if you need predictable latency):
- 30-day mini-reservation with guaranteed concurrency slab and an applied 10% rebate if you sign full Pilot within 30 days.
- Priced as a light reserved SKU; proposal requires procurement approval.

I’ve looped Karthik to confirm if we can waive the evaluation surcharge under a conversion path and David for a quick ops check on feasibility. I’ll attach a draft termsheet (Greenline_POC_Termsheet_v2.pdf) with numbers.

Which option should I formalize?

Best,
Hiro
